title: 180-degree hairpin grip versus drift comparison
description: 180-degree turn, 30 m radius, 18 m/s entry, 12 m width from BENCHMARKS.md 'Handling fixtures' (Hairpin row). BENCHMARKS asks for hairpin deltas to be reported rather than gated, so this fixture carries a reporting metric only. Approach and exit lengths are authored initial values.

geometry.start_reference: World origin at the start of segment 0 on the centerline; forward -Z, right +X, up +Y.

segments.note: Authored approach length; BENCHMARKS specifies radius, angle, width and entry speed only.
Arc length r*theta = 94.2478 m. Turn direction is an authored initial value.

runs.description: 18 m/s entry on the scripted drift controller.

driver.note: Controller implementation is M1 work; the revision identifier is reserved, not yet assigned.

runs.description: 18 m/s entry on the scripted grip controller; same entry conditions as the drift run.

timing_gates.purpose: Approach start; entry speed is measured here.

expected_events.note: Grip returns over about 0.35 s without snapping (GAME_DESIGN); recovery quality is reviewed from telemetry, not gated here.

comparison.purpose: Report the hairpin delta between the drift and grip lines for the three starters at stock and maximum upgrades.

metrics.name: hairpin_elapsed_time_delta
metrics.description: BENCHMARKS asks for hairpin deltas to be reported alongside the sweeper target; no percentage threshold is claimed for the hairpin.

cars.note: BENCHMARKS handling comparisons use all three starters at stock and maximum upgrades.

unknowns.reason: The scripted drift controller is M1 work; its revision identifier is reserved but not yet assigned.
The scripted grip controller is M1 work; its revision identifier is reserved but not yet assigned.
car.balanced_starter is the fixed ID of the balanced starter (Comet) from BENCHMARKS; the Sparrow and Slidewinder IDs are working names until the M1 car registry assigns stable IDs.

The per-car handling resource (../handling_config.schema.json) is M1 work; the revision this fixture targets is undetermined until M1 assigns it. BENCHMARKS regenerates reference records when handling dependencies change, so the fixture records the target revision instead of duplicating coefficients.
